title.narrative: Skills for Inclusive Growth Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The program is aligned with the following impact: government strategies to achieve inclusive growth through improved workforce skills and productivity in the country's key economic sectors, specifically the National Sustainable Development Strategy, 2013-2017; Education Development Strategy, 2012-2020; and the new Regional Policy of the Kyrgyz Republic 2018-2022. The program will have the following outcome: an established market-responsive, entrepreneurial, and inclusive TVET system. The program includes three outputs: (i) TVET governance and finance strengthened, (ii) teaching quality and learning environments improved, and (iii) cooperation with industry increased and entrepreneurship skills developed.

description.narrative: A market-responsive, entrepreneurial, and inclusive TVET system established

Employability of graduates in priority occupations increased by 30% in supported COEs (including 5% self-employment), of which at least 30% are female and 60% come from secondary cities (2018 baseline: To be established) Achievement: 76 Progress/Status: Likely to be achieved. Employability of graduates in 16 project's priority occupations in supported COEs increased by 61.45% (127 females (17.84%) out of 712 students employed in 2023). According to a survey conducted by the colleges, the number of graduates who started their own business is 211 students, which makes up 4% of the total number of graduates. Out of 8 project's COEs 6 are located in the secondary cities. Employed graduates of those 6 COEs are 534 (75% of the total number of employed graduates from 8 COEs). Data Source: MOES tracer studies and employability measurement approach

Number of graduates in priority occupations increased by 30%, of which at least 30% are female (2018 baseline: To be established) Achievement: 146 Progress/Status: Likely to be achieved. Number of graduates in priority occupations increased by 92% (890 graduates) of which 241 (27.1%) are female. Data Source: MOES graduation statistics

Employer satisfaction with TVET graduates increased by 5% (2014 baseline: N/A) Achievement: 54.8 Progress/Status: Achieved. The CAICO study of 601 respondents (employers) identified a positive trend: the respondents' satisfaction improved by 24.8% (from 33% to 57.8%). Data Source: Surveys of employers
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Cooperation with industry increased and entrepreneurship skills developed Indicator: Entrepreneurship training makes up at least 10% of hours taught in all supported COEs across all subjects, and makes up at least 5% of hours taught in each individual subject (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: In 2021, the “Entrepreneurship” textbook received the MOES KR stamp and recommendation as SVET training material for inclusion as a separate humanitarian discipline in pilot specialty training programs, which amounted to more than 5%. Entrepreneurship competencies make at least 10% of the occupational cycle in priority specialty training materials / programs. Data Source: Expert council mandate and cooperation agreements, memorandums of understanding, business plans, syllabi, and media items

Output: Cooperation with industry increased and entrepreneurship skills developed Indicator: Expert groups, with at least 20% female membership, for industry partnerships established and operational in each supported COE by 2019 (2017 baseline: 0 expert groups) Achievement: 48 Progress/Status: Achieved. MOES established the composition of the expert groups by its Order 462/1 dated June 17, 2020. Out of 139 expert group members in 2020, 55 (39%) were females. Out of 153 expert group members in 2023, 73 (48%) were females. Expert groups were established in every COE. Data Source: Expert council mandate and cooperation agreements, memorandums of understanding, business plans, syllabi, and media items

Output: Cooperation with industry increased and entrepreneurship skills developed Indicator: Supported COEs have established at least 15 formal industry partnerships by 2022 (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: To establish sustainable partnerships with potential employers, it was proposed that colleges receive social partnership training and, subsequently, sign agreements of a new format, which provides for broader cooperation. In Q1 2021, a public signing of memorandums took place in each college with the participation of deputy mayors, heads of city social development departments, university rectors, prominent industry representatives. Local and national media covered the process extensively. Data Source: Expert council mandate and cooperation agreements, memorandums of understanding, business plans, syllabi, and media items

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: National qualifications system (including national qualifications framework) developed and agreed between line ministries and stakeholders by 2021 (2017 baseline: Not applicable) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: "The Government of the Kyrgyz Republic (GOK KR) approved the “Concept of the National Qualifications System of the Kyrgyz Republic (Decree No. 505; September 30, 2019). GOK KR approved the “Implementation Action Plan for the National Qualifications System for 2020-2021” (Order No. 79-r; March 16, 2020). GOK KR approved the “National Qualifications Framework” (Decree No. 491; September 18, 2020)."
Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports Actual value: Y

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: Skills development forms integral part of both the country's long-term approved and implemented development strategy and the corresponding education strategy by 2021 (2017 baseline: Not applicable) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: "The President of the Kyrgyz Republic signed the Decree “On the National Development Strategy of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2018 - 2040” that reflects the need for skills development (November 1, 2018). The Government of the Kyrgyz Republic approved the Education Development Program of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2021-2040 and is Implementation Action Plan for 2021-2023 (Decree No. 200; May 4, 2021). Section V “Education Priorities” of the Program covers issues of improving the vocational education system, inclusivity, effective learning environment, modernization, quality training materials, and per capita funding."
Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports Actual value: Y

Output: Teaching quality and learning environments improved Indicator: 5,000 students (both self- and state-financed) trained in priority occupations or specializations in supported COEs and 950 students in aligned primary TVET lyceums by 2022 (15% female, 2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 1363 Progress/Status: Achieved. 5,731 students (811 females - 14,2%) were trained in priority specializations in supported COEs and 2,162 students (329 females - 15.2%) were trained in priority occupations in the aligned primary TVET lyceums. Data Source: MOES approval documents, standards, curricula, and training materials

Output: Teaching quality and learning environments improved Indicator: 500 primary TVET and 2,500 secondary TVET teachers, of which are 30% female, report improved skills in pedagogic and technical areas by 2020 Achievement: 615 Progress/Status: Achieved. Out of 6,958 teachers trained (1,845 PVET teachers and 5,113 SVET teachers) 4,972 were females. Data Source: MOES approval documents, standards, curricula, and training materials

Output: Teaching quality and learning environments improved Indicator: Curricula and training materials developed based on job profiles and validated by industry representatives for 15 occupations or specializations in at least five supported COEs (2017 baseline: Not applicable) Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: Facilitators/experts consulted Center of Excellence (COE) teachers and vocational lyceum stuffs on the development of training materials and the implementation of modular training. The materials have been developed for 15 specializations and trainings have been conducted in all pilot educational institutions (8 COEs and 9 lyceums). Data Source: MOES approval documents, standards, curricula, and training materials

Output: Teaching quality and learning environments improved Indicator: Eight colleges upgraded to COEs by 2021 (three in secondary cities) (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: Achieved. MOES approved 8 colleges as COEs (Order No. 1056/1; September 5, 2019). MOES issued an Order “On Approval of the Guidelines for Transforming Colleges into Centers of Excellence” (No. 462/1; June 19, 2020). Out of 8 project's COEs 6 are located in the secondary cities. Data Source: MOES approval documents, standards, curricula, and training materials

Output: Teaching quality and learning environments improved Indicator: WBL concept piloted in 15 priority occupations or specializations by 2020 (5,000 students by 2024; of which are 15% female; 2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: Likely to be achieved. WBL concept have been approved in 2019 and piloted in 8 COEs for 16 priority specializations (5,731 students (811 females - 14,2%)
Data Source: MOES approval documents, standards, curricula, and training materials

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: At least eight local industry mapping studies finalized by COEs using MOES- and MOLSD-approved methodology (2018 baseline: 0) and each supported COE introduces at least one new or revised occupation or specialization each academic year, starting in 2019, based on results of industry mapping studies (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 8 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. 32 local industry mapping studies finalized by COEs using MOES and MOLSD approved methodology. Each supported COE introduced from 4 to 12 new occupations during 2019-2023 but not every COE introduced 1 new occupation or specialization each academic year (2 out of 8 did not achieve): COE Jalal-Abad College (11 new occupations); COE Naryn Agroeconomic College (4); COE Issyk-Kul Industrial Pedagogical College (5); COE Tokmok College (6); COE Kyzyl-Kiya Mining College of Economics and Innovation (12); COE Bishkek College of Architecture and Management in Construction (3); COE Osh Industrial and Pedagogical College (6); COE Kara-Balta Technical and Economic College (6); Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: Recognition of prior learning in at least 10 priority occupations or specializations from primary TVET to secondary TVET; with pilot starting in 2021 (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved. All 17 PVET organizations covered by the project have transferred to the credit educational system, which helps colleges/COEs recognize prior learning including 16 priority occupations. Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: At least 5,000 trainees trained under the Skills Development Fund, of which 30% are women (2016 baseline: 600) Achievement: 3318 Progress/Status: SDF organized training: between 2016 and 2018 for 17,503 people; in 2019 for 5,195 people (44.7% - women); in 2020, due to COVID-19 restrictions for only 117 people; in 2021 for 543 people (47% women), and in 2022 for 3,318 people (48% women). Thus, during its work with the SISGSDP (2019 - 2022), the SDF had 9,173 people trained. It should be noted that, in 2019, the Project provided financing for short-term SDF courses, and since 2020 - only for the staff of the Fund. The SIGSDP stopped funding the SDF in 2023, when the Fund was made part of the Ministry of Labor, Social Security and Migration.
Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports

Output: TVET governance and finance strengthened Indicator: EMIS implemented for evidence-based policymaking in all primary TVET institutes and in 75% of secondary TVET institutes by 2021 (2017 baseline: 75% in primary TVET, 19% in secondary TVET, including gender disaggregated data collection) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. EMIS was implemented in 99 PVET and 150 SVET organizations. 100% of PVET organizations are providing statistical data in EMIS and 139 SVET organizations (92.6% out of 150 SVET) are providing statistical data in EMIS including gender disaggregated data collection. Data Source: National and education strategies, guidelines, handbook, government gazette, training plans, charter, organigram of MOES, decree, regulations, sublegal acts, enrollment statistics, and EMIS reports
